problem.title: Your kid is already using AI. Are they using it well?
problem.p1: AI is everywhere. In homework apps, in games, in their friends' phones. Most kids are figuring it out alone, and they're picking up bad habits fast.
problem.p2: Schools are still catching up. Most classrooms won't teach AI literacy for years. By then, the wrong reflexes are already locked in.
problem.p3: AI met Spark gives your child the right foundation now: how to spot AI mistakes, protect their secrets, and use AI as a brain booster instead of a shortcut.

about.title: Spark is free — and that's not by accident
about.subtitle: The story of a dad who went looking for something for his own kids — and built it himself.
about.sparkBubble: Hi! I'm Spark. But this was Ferry's idea. Read along?
paragraphs: I'm Ferry Hoes. Speaker, author, AI expert. But above all, I'm the dad of two small kids growing up in a world that's about to run on AI and automation.
They're still young. They don't yet understand what that means. But I do.

I travel the world telling companies and governments how to handle AI. I founded the AI Literacy Academy so professionals understand what AI is, what it can do, and what it can't. I write about it. I speak about it. It's my craft.
But at home, at the kitchen table, I had nothing.
I was looking for something to teach my own kids what AI really is. How it works. When to trust it and when not. How to stay in charge of a tool that acts smart but doesn't actually think.
It didn't exist. Not in their language. Not for their age. Not in a way that matches how they experience the world.
AI met Spark is free, because I want every kid to be able to use it. No matter the size of their parents' wallet. This knowledge shouldn't be a luxury.
Spark is the guide I wanted for my own kids. And now he's here for your kid too.
